Modest practical boxy metal body, separate rectangular framed windows, a low pale gray roof following the incline, stepped passenger compartments appropriate to a funicular. It sits firmly ON two rails along a continuous steep downhill railway, aligned exactly with the rails. It is a rail-based cable-hauled vehicle, not a suspended cable-car, bus, tram on a street, or flat-floor modern panoramic train. All surfaces plain and unbranded.
Clear physical evacuation arrangement: one short portable exit ladder with just a few treads is visibly hooked securely to an OPEN SIDE DOOR of the stopped car; its feet rest on a small stable landing directly beside the track. This short exit ladder is physically connected to the car door, not floating or detached. Beside the same side of the rails is a separate continuous narrow stairway, with low practical handrail, running ALONG THE TRACK DOWN THE HILL toward the city. The landing joins this trackside stairway directly. Preserve a coherent route from the car door to the ladder, to the landing, to the stairway.

MIDDLE FUNCTION ZONE: three successive simple domestic levels, with original generic 16th-century furnishings spread naturally across them: unadorned wooden bench and table, an ordinary stone fireplace, and a plain tiled stove. Modest worn wood, no fine art, no period replica sculpture, no heraldry. Every furnishing is an invented period-plausible generic design, not an actual object now in a museum.
UPPER FUNCTION ZONE: one upper cannon room just beneath a shallow mostly empty attic. Two small static plain dark iron cannons on simple timber carriages sit safely indoors, their barrels aligned toward modest external embrasures at the SIDE walls. These are generic invented historical defence fixtures, not collection replicas. No firing, no smoke, no projectile, no people or soldiers.
Composition/framing: almost straight frontal view, with a subtle natural perspective into the opened rooms. The complete tall tower and low turf roof fill most of the image height, centred on the 3:2 canvas with calm gray sky at the sides. All broad functions are legible without labels; use realistic subdued daylight reaching the cut rooms, darkest at the dungeon and slightly brighter at the roof. Show the thick cut stone side edges clearly.
Style/medium: camera-captured natural material appearance applied to a conceptual architectural section. Crisp natural rubble stone, weathered timber, plain tile and iron surfaces; muted stone gray, dull brown, earth and turf green. Soft honest overcast daylight, restrained contrast. No HDR, no cinematic grading, no shiny CGI, no ink drawing, no pencil lines, no painted illustration, no measurement diagram.
Avoid: text, numerals, letters, captions, labels, signs, floor-number markers, plans, measurement lines, writing, logos, watermark, signature, border, flags, insignia, artworks, museum exhibits, modern fixtures, tourists, ANY human, recognizable face, prison victim, blood, violence, skulls, fired weapons. No later 1620s full-covering high roof.
